merged.title: feat(rac3): Up Your Arsenal native port (development build)
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
Ratchet & Clank: Up Your Arsenal (PAL and NTSC-U) as a native port, at functional parity with Going Commando's. It is a development build, behind the launcher's Settings → Developer → "Up Your Arsenal (development)" switch.

## What it does
- **Boot and front end:** native 2D (wrapped routines, distance-field font) and Widget3D panels. Options include the Video page; languages (PAL), saves and load, launcher Play, and the save editor all work. Checked against retail footage.
- **Levels:** every single-player level loads its program, and all 27 reach control in the regression tour (`regress.py --game rac3-pal --set rac3-tour`). Veldin plays from start to exit, and the ship flight carries Ratchet to Florana.
- **Rendering:** native world, ties, shrubs, sky, mobys with poses, particles, effect quads, water, shadows and the loading flight. Also chrome and glass, glow and bangles, Ratchet's looks, enhanced lighting (probe GI, cascades, GTAO), texture packs, draw distance, the occlusion mask

merged.title: feat(baker): place lighting probes with layered watershed
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

- Use the same layered free-space basins to place oriented GI grids and reflection influence volumes. Fit multiple volumes to large or winding basins and share reflection captures across a basin’s volumes.
- Weight reflection blending by surface facing and audit surface coverage without adding volumes.
- Tile the watershed graph for larger levels and add an offline inspector for basins, portals, volume fitting and failed placements.
- Support rotated, LZ4-compressed GI seed files and preserve bake publication when optional watershed diagnostics fail to write.

## Verification

- Built the baker, enhanced viewer and affected test binaries on Windows with Vulkan enabled.
- Ran nine CTest entries covering the native bake pipeline, watershed, volume fitting, room routes and Vulkan probe rendering. All passed.
- Passed port conventions, layering, host-hook parity and the Python seed tests.
- Verified all 21 R&C1 NTSC exports in 6m 55s before the rebase. R&C2 full-batch, PAL game

merged.title: fix(port): preserve Vulkan render graph state across passes
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

- Make single-subresource Vulkan images visible to shader stages that sample them in later graphs.
- Keep discarded contents undefined after partial writes. Apply discards at the first live use so interrupted work preserves later images.
- Report render worker failures with the frame, submission site, exception type, and message. Give scene recording its own state and capture the snapshot directly in the job.

## Verification

- Rebuilt RAC1 NTSC and ran the render worker, immediate graph work, graph attachment, and native command boundary tests. Enabled Vulkan synchronization validation for the GPU tests.
- Passed frame graph, Vulkan presentation, Vulkan failure, and direct-render Vulkan tests.
- Passed strict port conventions against `origin/develop`, port layering, and RAC1/RAC2 host-hook parity checks.
- Completed 420-frame RAC1 NTSC title-screen smoke tests on Windows Vulkan with the render worker enabled and disabled. PAL gameplay and other graphics platforms were out

merged.title: feat(port): select world depth from device support
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

- Select Precise depth when the active backend supports 32-bit float depth-stencil and zero-to-one clip depth. Otherwise use Normal depth and move the near plane from 0.05 to 0.25 only when the backend can clamp depth.
- Rasterize object motion vectors in the same clip space as the world depth buffer. This fixes visible smearing on sideways movement in RAC1 with FSR and motion blur active.
- Cover depth-format selection and rejection of occluded object motion in GPU regression tests. There is no user-facing setting.

## Verification

- Built Windows RAC1 NTSC and RAC2 NTSC with the enhanced preset. All 19 local checks passed, including the Vulkan render-equivalence runs, depth-format tests, FSR motion and motion blur.
- Exercised desktop OpenGL and OpenGL ES with clip control enabled and hidden. On Metropolis, compared scripted left and right movement with FSR and motion blur enabled and verified the lighting bake loaded.
- Pinned formatting and layering checks passed. Loca

merged.author: nickyyOO

merged.title: feat(rac2): more room for spawned mobys, interface 1.27
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
Going Commando's spawned mobys (bolts, shots, effects, mods' enemy copies) come from a pool of spare slots the level's file sets (n2, 200 to 400; Barlow 398). With none free a spawn is lost, a bolt with it. NG++'s Barlow copies take 79 of them; a flood of 300 pickups there made 228 (box1, hidden runs).

- Interface 1.27: moby_pool_raise(extra) (up to 512 more slots in every level loaded from then on) and moby_pool_status (in all, alive, free, added). The count is raised as the loader's WadDecompress ends (host/moby_pool.c), the way rac1's bigger pool is; OPENRAC_MOBY_EXTRA=N does the same from the environment.
- With +400 on Barlow all 300 of the flood were made and collectable; the table is 1,505 slots, the pool 798.
- OPENRAC_PLAY_TRACE: mobys, coins, killnear, flood=N, drop=N.
- Copies on a 1.26 port match their originals in state, update, flags and distances (checked with mobys,copies).

merged.title: fix(rac2): build the movie's list in the movie's buffers
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
Before: the port's movie player ignored the buffer pool the game passes to PlayFmvMovie, so g_movie_buffer_base stayed 0. Each blank's list (picture sprites and subtitles) was written at 0x1C81C0 itself, over game data. On Jamming Array the map state sits there, so the save after the last Fizzwidget scene read a broken map mask and ran off the end of RAM (crash at 0x02000000).

After: the list goes to pool + 0x1C81C0, as on the console. Nothing at 0x1C81C0 changes during a movie.

How: func_0034EF58 sets the base to the pool while the movie plays and back to 0 after, like the retail function (0x34EF60, 0x34F030). Shared host C, so NTSC, NTSC v2 and PAL all get it.

Tested: crash report symbolized with the 1.1.0 build; in the container (NTSC-U) checked the list address and the memory at 0x1C81C0 before and after a movie, a boot to the first level with movies on, ctest rac2 host tables, call ABI and parity, conventions check. merged.author: nickyyOO

merged.title: fix(port): use single-sample Enhanced Graphics and set preset render scales
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

- Use one sample per pixel whenever Enhanced Graphics is selected, including when temporal upscaling is off or probe lighting is still loading. Keep the saved MSAA setting for standard graphics.

merged.title: feat(sdk): lock the mod ABI so it only grows
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** nothing checks the whole mod ABI. Only a few `offsetof` checks in tests. A moved table member, a changed struct field or a changed constant would break every built mod, and CI might not notice.

**After:** `sdk/api/` holds three generated locks: the `openrac_api` table (place, offset, type of each member), every public struct and typedef, and every `OPENRAC_` macro. A row never changes or goes. CI fails when the headers break that.

**How:** `sdk/tools/gen_api_lock.py` reads the C headers with clang (AST for types, a small built program for offsets, `-dM` for macros). It refuses to write a lock that changes or drops a row. `--check` runs in `sdk.yml`; on a pull request `--against` also holds the headers to the base branch's locks, so a hand-edited lock can't hide a break. Only `OPENRAC_MOD_API_MINOR` and `OPENRAC_MOD_TARGET_MINOR` may change value.

merged.title: fix(rac2): Mini-Nuke blasts stop after the second shot in PAL
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
Before: in PAL, from the third Mini-Nuke shot the blast plays its sound but deals no damage and shows no fire. The Maktar arena challenge with 8 Mini-Nuke shots could not be finished.

After: every shot explodes, as on the disc.

How: hostgen read a suffixed level name that the release table leaves out (D_L00_001B060C_1, the blast pointer) as the executable's D_001B060C, which is another datum. The pointer was never cleared, so each new blast deleted itself. Such a name now keeps its own address. This also corrects about 14 other PAL and v2.00 data references; each was checked against the retail level dumps. NTSC v1.00 and rac1 output does not change.

Tested: PAL Maktar run, 8 of 8 blasts (2 before). New hostgen test; test_hostgen.py and test_release_rac2.py pass.

merged.title: ci: run the locked Vulkan tests on a fourth runner
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
Before: most Vulkan tests share one lock, so the "vulkan" test runner ran them one by one, about 17 minutes after the Enhanced build. That chain (build + vulkan tests, about 38 minutes cold) was the slowest path of checks.

After: tests that need only the cache reset (GTAO, rim, normals, local lights, water, wetness and a few more) run on a new "effects" runner. The vulkan runner should drop to about 10-11 minutes and effects take about 7. Same tests, same lock, same checks; only the machine differs.

Also: hostgen caches ctype.parse. The same type strings were parsed millions of times. hostgen is 2-15% faster (rac2-ntsc 211 s to 180 s in a 4-core container); the generated C is byte for byte the same for rac1-pal, rac2-ntsc and rac2-pal.

How: tools/ci_port_tests.py gets a THIRD_RUNNER set and stops the plan if one of those tests ever needs another fixture. checks.yml gets the fourth matrix row.

Tested: hostgen tests (359), tools/test_ci_*.py, new tools/test_ci_port_tests.py, conventi

opened.author: Clank700
opened.untrustedBody:
## Summary

A prop is a rigid mesh: a mod can place it but not deform it, so anything with moving parts (a creature, a cloth, a rig of its own) cannot be shown. Add prop_set_skin(mod, id, joint_matrices, count): the mod gives one 4 x 4 matrix per joint each tick and the renderer draws the prop's glTF skin deformed by them, as it draws the game's own characters. Without a skin, or with count 0, the prop is drawn in its bind pose as before.

## How

Convention (documented in the header): joint j's matrix takes a vertex as stored, in the mesh's own coordinates, to where that joint puts it, so the identity is the bind pose and a matrix is the joint's pose times the inverse of its bind pose. A joint is numbered by its node name (joint_12 is 12); other names take the place in the skin's joints array. Matrices must be finite and at most OPENRAC_PROP_JOINTS_MAX.

opened.author: Clank700
opened.untrustedBody:
## Summary

An overlay can only lay a colour over the frame with alpha. A mod cannot add light to the picture (a glow, a flash) or take colour away from it (a darkening, a shadow, a "negative" glow), which the game's own effects do. Add openrac_overlay.set_blend(context, blend) with OPENRAC_OVERLAY_BLEND_ALPHA (the default, unchanged), _ADD (dst + src * a) and _SUBTRACT (dst - src * a, held at 0).

## How

set_blend says how the rect and text calls after it go over the frame, until the next call. Each mod's callback starts as ALPHA whatever another mod's callback left, so a mod needs to know nothing of the others. A blend the port does not have is refused (the call answers 0 and the last blend stays), never drawn some other way. The frame's own alpha is kept by all three. The set of blends is open: a new one is a new value, not a new function.

opened.author: Clank700
opened.untrustedBody:
## Summary

A mod that wants a jolt or a landing shake has no way to use the game's own: it can move the camera itself (camera_set) but then has to take the whole camera, and the shake would not match the game's own. Add camera_shake(mod, channel, amplitude, frames), which starts the game's shake on the level's camera, the one its landings and blows use.

## How

Channel 0 moves the eye along the camera's up row, 1 along its forward row. The amplitude is 0 to 1 and the count 0 to OPENRAC_CAMERA_SHAKE_FRAMES_MAX (600) game ticks, converted as the game's scale_ticks does; the game's own apply_camera_shake decays it and 0 stops the channel. A new call replaces the channel's shake. A bad channel, amplitude or count, or no level, answers OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN and never reaches the host. It ends with the level.

## Summary

A mod that wants something from another installed game (a texture or a model of a sibling title, for a crossover) has no path to its data: the port only tells a mod about the game it is running. Add game_data_dir(mod, game, out, size): the player's data folder of an installed game (<install>/active/<game>/data, the same layout as the running game's own), read only.

Reading another game is a permission the mod asks for, not a default: the manifest lists the games in a new "reads_games" array, and a game not listed answers the new OPENRAC_HOOK_REFUSED (-6). The running game needs no entry. The call returns the path's length, 0 when the game is not installed or extracted (or the id is not a game id: letters, digits and dashes, at most 32), and OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN when the port cannot say (a data folder it did not get from the launcher's layout, or a buffer that is too small: nothing is written then).

opened.author: Clank700
opened.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Levels carry baked camera visibility (which zones can be seen from where), and the renderer culls with it. It is correct for the camera the game made. A mod that moves the camera (camera_set), or a mod that changes what is shown, sees through it: geometry the baked set says is out of sight is not drawn, so the picture has holes. Add camera_visibility_bypass(mod, enabled): while it is on, the gameplay view uses frustum and depth culling alone, without the baked set.

## How

It is a request, not a mode: enabled 1 is taken only in a level in play (anything else answers OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN), 0 gives it back, and it goes with the level load or the mod's unload. Several mods may ask; the bypass is on while any of them holds it. The camera pose is untouched. The cost is drawing what the set would have culled, so a mod should ask only for the camera angles or regions that need it.

opened.author: nickyyOO
opened.untrustedBody:
**Before:** nothing checks the whole mod ABI. Only a few `offsetof` checks in tests. A moved table member, a changed struct field or a changed constant would break every built mod, and CI might not notice.

**After:** `sdk/api/` holds three generated locks: the `openrac_api` table (place, offset, type of each member), every public struct and typedef, and every `OPENRAC_` macro. A row never changes or goes. CI fails when the headers break that.

**How:** `sdk/tools/gen_api_lock.py` reads the C headers with clang (AST for types, a small built program for offsets, `-dM` for macros). It refuses to write a lock that changes or drops a row. `--check` runs in `sdk.yml`; on a pull request `--against` also holds the headers to the base branch's locks, so a hand-edited lock can't hide a break. Only `OPENRAC_MOD_API_MINOR` and `OPENRAC_MOD_TARGET_MINOR` may change value.

merged.title: Add 10 near misses that are exact only with inline asm (plzcw, blezl abs)
merged.author: farfeduc
merged.untrustedBody:
Ten main-image functions (each in 14 level places under the same name) compile to retail's bytes, but only with two inline asm helpers. CONTRIBUTING.md and `docs/agents/levers.md` do not allow inline asm in matched C, so they go to `nonmatching/` as near misses, not `src/`.

**Why inline asm**
- **plzcw** (leading sign bits, used as floor/ceil log2 of texture sizes): SN 2.95.3 has `__builtin_plzcw`, but it works on 128-bit values and adds `por` copies and a sign extension. No C form gives retail's bare `plzcw`. About 25 main-image functions use it.
- **abs written `blezl x; sub x, $0, x`**: GCC's abs is `bltzl` + `negu`, and no compiler in `toolchain/` has a `blezl` pattern. The disassembler already marks this `neg` as a handwritten instruction (func_00493888). About 10 functions use it.

So the original source had inline asm here. If maintainers want an exception for instructions the compiler cannot emit (for example one small header with the two helpers), these ten can move to `src/`

Fixes #268.

The `mateuszklysz/RAC-Board` repo is now `nickyyOO/RAC-Board`. The old account no longer exists, so this looks like a username rename. Every index build failure since 2026-11-19 23:44 UTC fails on this entry:

```
error: index/rac-board.json: https://api.github.com/repos/mateuszklysz/RAC-Board/releases?per_page=100&page=1: rate limited for 1891 s
```

**Why it says "rate limited":** the old API URL returns a 301 to `/repositories/1441966685/...`. `Http._open` attaches the token with `add_unredirected_header`, so the redirected request goes out without it. Requests without a token are limited per IP, and runner IPs are shared, so that limit is often already used up. The wait is then over 900 s and the build gives up. Builds pass or fail depending on the runner's IP, which is why it's intermittent. Other repos in the same run fetch fine.
